newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DyStar eyes Clariant unit, but no move seen.
newsitem.headline: German DyStar eyes Clariant unit, but no move seen.

text.p: Germany's DyStar GmbH said on Tuesday that it would be interested in obtaining the textile dyestuff business from Swiss specialty chemicals group Clariant AG but that it was not in a position to make a decision.
"We are interested, but the decision making process rests with someone else," DyStar general manager Alfred Rad told a news conference.

DyStar, the world's leading textile dyestuff company, which is jointly owned by German chemical giants Bayer AG and Hoechst AG was thrust into a precarious position when Hoechst last year obtained a 45 percent stake in DyStar's competitor Clariant.
"We now have the situation that Hoechst owns a stake in two direct competitors," Rad said.
Rad however declined to make any further comment on the issue or its possible outcome.
Clariant was not immediately available for comment.
A Hoechst spokesman said that any competition issues arising between the two companies would have to be settled by these companies and that Hoechst had no plans to get involved in the situation.
Currently DyStar, posting annual sales of 1.6 billion marks ($944.8 million), ranks as the world's largest dyestuff company followed by German BASF AG and Swiss groups Ciba and Clariant.
